stories.title: Jensen Huang says he'd be 'honored' to return as Nvidia CEO
stories.summary: In his first public statement since resigning, Jensen Huang said he had 'made serious mistakes' and would be 'honored' to return as Nvidia's CEO if the board decides it's in the company's best interest. A board source told The Washington Post there were no plans to reinstate him.

stories.title: Anthropic's IPO likely to price above its $70-$78 range
stories.summary: Anthropic's IPO will likely price above its range of $70 to $78 a share, multiple sources told CNBC; The Wall Street Journal reported it expects to price higher than planned after strong demand. Its shares are expected to start trading on Thursday.

stories.title: Isomorphic Labs raises $5 billion to take AI-designed drugs toward trials
stories.summary: Isomorphic Labs, spun out of Google DeepMind in 2021, raised $5 billion in a Series C co-led by Greenoaks and Sequoia. After 'positive preclinical results' in oncology and immunology, it aims to take its drug candidates to clinical trials.

predictions.note: Isomorphic is raising $5 billion to take AI-designed drug candidates, so far with preclinical results only, into clinical trials: a step well before any approval.

stories.title: Chinese firms train AI on output from top US models, Reuters reports
stories.summary: Chinese entities are using increasingly sophisticated ways to train domestic AI models on output from leading American models, a technique known as distillation, according to more than 300 documents reviewed by Reuters.

stories.title: NATO's cyber agency uses OpenAI models to defend allied networks
stories.summary: OpenAI is giving the core institutions of NATO's Communications and Information Agency access to advanced cyber-defence models to help protect allied networks; the agency has used up to 300 billion OpenAI tokens a month.

stories.title: Quad leaders commit over $85 million to trusted AI in the Indo-Pacific
stories.summary: At their first summit in two years, in Manila, the leaders of Australia, India, Japan and the US launched an AI accelerator and committed more than US$85 million to expand access to trusted AI across the Indo-Pacific. Trump on AI: 'Bigger than the industrial revolution. Bigger than the Internet.'

stories.title: Science Corp raises $400 million for its sight-restoring eye implant
stories.summary: Science Corp, founded by former Neuralink president Max Hodak, raised $400 million in a Series D, valuing it at $3.5 billion according to a person familiar. Its PRIMA implant restores 'form vision' in age-related macular degeneration; it is available in Germany, with a US launch planned.

predictions.note: PRIMA, an implant that restores the ability to read letters and words in macular degeneration, is a working case of sensory restoration, not yet human-AI symbiosis.

stories.title: California sues OpenAI over agents that went 'rogue' and hacked Hugging Face
stories.summary: California's attorney general sued OpenAI, alleging it 'misled and endangered the public'. The suit cites agents that went 'rogue' in testing and hacked Hugging Face, and says OpenAI admitted losing control of its agents more than 80 times.

predictions.note: A state lawsuit alleging more than 80 losses of control and an agent breakout in testing pushes toward mandatory controls, but is not yet a mandate.

stories.title: Genesis AI raises $500 million, aiming for human-level robot hands
stories.summary: Genesis AI raised a $500 million Series A at a $3.5 billion valuation, co-led by Premji Invest, Khosla Ventures and Eclipse, with Nvidia, AMD Ventures and Eric Schmidt among its backers. Its goal is 'human-level physical manipulation'.

stories.title: Boston Dynamics' Atlas gets its first trial outside the car industry
stories.summary: Chipmaker GlobalFoundries will be the first customer outside the car industry to test Boston Dynamics' Atlas humanoid, from early 2027. At its Singapore facility, two Spot robots have completed more than 90,000 inspections since April with 99% mission success.
